scenes.title: What if the Sun disappeared?
scenes.narration: What if the Sun disappeared right now? When would we notice?

scenes.title: An impossible thought experiment
scenes.narration: This is impossible under known physics. Still, imagining this event reveals how much our planet depends on the Sun.

scenes.title: Eight minutes of sunlight
scenes.narration: Sunlight takes about eight minutes to reach Earth. During that time, we would still see light already traveling through space.

scenes.title: Daylight would disappear
scenes.narration: Then daylight would disappear. The Moon would also lose its reflected sunlight. Distant stars would remain visible across the dark sky.

scenes.title: Earth would keep moving
scenes.narration: A change in gravity would also travel at the speed of light. Earth would then move approximately along the tangent to its orbit.

scenes.title: Cooling would take time
scenes.narration: The surface would start cooling, but not all at once. Oceans, air and land would still hold heat, slowing the initial temperature drop.

scenes.title: Food webs would change
scenes.narration: Without sunlight, photosynthesis would stop. Plants, animals and people would face a spreading crisis across food webs.

scenes.title: Some life uses chemical energy
scenes.narration: Surprisingly, not all life depends directly on sunlight. Some deep ocean ecosystems use chemical energy from reactions near hydrothermal vents.

scenes.title: Energy beneath our feet
scenes.narration: Heat inside Earth would remain. Shelters with reliable energy could help people, but survival would demand resources and careful planning.

scenes.title: Our star makes a difference
scenes.narration: Without the Sun, our world would change. Had you imagined this dependence?
